collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: Angry customers, losing trust, my business reputation tanking. Who's controlling this thing? I need real humans, not robots.

transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — there’s a lot of AI junk out there right now.  

So before I even try to “convince” you… what were you hoping this would actually do for your business when you clicked on it?
User: How do I know this isn't just some robot calling my customers and messing up my business?
Agent: Totally fair worry — if it messed up your customer calls, it’d be useless.  

When you picture it “messing up your business,” what’s the nightmare scenario in your head — angry customers, missed leads, wrong info, something else?
User: Angry customers, losing trust, my business reputation tanking. Who's controlling this thing? I need real humans, not robots.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — if it risks your reputation, it’s not worth it.  

So just to be clear: are you mostly worried about it talking to *existing* customers, or more about it handling *new* inbound leads when you can’t pick up?
User: Both, honestly. I don't want it screwing up with new leads or annoying my existing customers.
Agent: Got it, that’s completely reasonable — both of those are your lifeblood.  

So I can explain how we keep a tight “safety net” around calls (what it can / can’t say, when a human jumps in), but first: what kind of business are you running?
User: I run a roofing business in Dallas. We miss about 30 calls a week while on jobs.
Agent: Got it — roofing in Dallas and about 30 calls a week slipping through while you’re on roofs, that’s real money walking.  

So when those 30 don’t reach you, what usually happens — do they leave voicemails and wait, or do they just hang up and call the next roofer?
User: Most hang up and call someone else. Voicemails are rare. It's frustrating losing potential jobs like that.
Agent: Yeah, that’s rough — if they don’t leave a voicemail, they’re basically gone.  

So with those 30 or so a week, how big are those jobs typically — are we talking a few hundred bucks each, or more like full roof replacements mixed in?
User: Average job's about $1,800. Losing 40% of those potential bookings hurts.
Agent: Yeah, losing 40% at eighteen hundred a pop adds up fast.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what that’s costing you in real dollars, or no one’s put the math in front of you yet?
User: No one's really broken it down for me, but I'm skeptical about any quick fixes you might offer.
Agent: Totally get being skeptical — you should be.  

With your own numbers, though, even landing 40% of those 30 missed calls at $1,800, that’s about $21,600 walking out the door every week while you’re on roofs and they’re calling another roofer instead… how does that hit you when you hear it that way?
User: That's a big chunk of change lost weekly. But who's ensuring this isn't just a scam to get my money?
Agent: Yeah, that’s a fair concern — especially with how much junk is out there right now.  

So setting the math aside for a second, what would you need to *see* or *hear* to feel like, “okay, this is legit, not some black-box robot wrecking my reputation”?
User: I need clear human interaction, full control over the process, and assurance my data stays private.
Agent: Makes total sense — you want real human-feeling calls, control, and privacy locked down.  

So starting with “control”: if this system only handled *missed* calls (when you don’t pick up), and you could decide exactly what it’s allowed to say and when it sends the caller to you or your office, would that feel safer?
User: That sounds more reasonable, but how can you guarantee my data and my customers' information stays private?
Agent: Yeah, totally fair to press on that.  

So, high level: calls are encrypted, data stays in a secure environment, and we don’t sell or share your customer info with third parties — would it help if I walk through exactly what gets stored (and what *doesn’t*) when a missed call is handled?
User: Alright, explain what data you store and what you don't. I'm listening, but still skeptical.
Agent: Totally fair to stay skeptical — I’d be the same.  

So, keeping it simple: on a missed call our system stores things like caller ID, call recording, basic transcript, and any booking details (name, address, appointment time); it does **not** store your card details, bank info, or sell/share your customer list with anyone — does that line up with what you were worried about, or is there a specific type of data you’re most nervous about?
User: Okay, that's somewhat reassuring. But how do I know the live call isn't just some pressure sales tactic?
Agent: Totally get that worry — nobody wants to get trapped in a hard-sell Zoom.  

The live call’s really just to walk through *your* numbers, show you exactly how missed calls would be handled for your roofing jobs, and then you decide yes/no with no pressure — if you saw it and hated it, would you feel comfortable just saying “no thanks” and walking away?
User: Alright, if there's truly no pressure and I can walk away, I might consider the live call.
Agent: Nice, that’s all I ask — come see it, keep your guard up, and walk away if it feels off.  

So we can set that up properly… what’s your first name?
User: It's Sam. But remember, I'm only agreeing to see how it works, not promising anything yet.
Agent: Got it, Sam — totally fine, this is just a look under the hood, nothing more.  

And your last name?
User: Ortiz. But remember, I'm only seeing how it works, not jumping in. What's the next step?
Agent: Perfect, Sam Ortiz, noted — and yes, you’re just coming to see it, nothing more.  

Next step is to grab your company name so we can tailor the walkthrough — what do you go by for the roofing business?
User: Ortiz Roofing. But make it clear, I'm just checking this out, not signing up for anything yet.
Agent: Perfect, Ortiz Roofing, and totally noted — you’re just checking it out, no commitment.  

And Sam, is the number you’re calling from right now the best contact number to reach you for the walkthrough?
User: No, my main number is +14695550001. Make sure not to spam or misuse it.
Agent: Got it, we’ll only use that for the walkthrough details and confirmation, no spam.  

Quick check, Sam — are you on Central time there in Dallas?
User: Yes, we're in Central Time here in Dallas. Just make sure it's a time that works for me.
Agent: Gotcha, we’ll keep it Central and make it work around your day, not mine.  

So first step: would you rather do the walkthrough later today, or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works better. Late afternoon would be ideal, so I can finish up my roofing jobs first.
Agent: Nice, tomorrow late afternoon works.  

I can get you in tomorrow at either 4:00 or 4:45 Central — which one’s better for you?
User: 4:45 Central works. Just remember, I'm only exploring this. No commitments.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: Sam, you’re all set for tomorrow at 4:45 Central — totally just an exploration, no commitments. You’ll get a text with the confirmation and a link in case you need to reschedule. Really glad you called in today; Jay’s looking forward to showing you how this would actually work for Ortiz Roofing. Have a great rest of your day, and we’ll talk tomorrow!
